notes: rust-stdlib-crypto over the RustCrypto cbc, cfb-mode, ctr, ofb and aes-gcm crates. Block, Stream, BlockMode and AEAD are traits (Block, Stream, BlockMode, Aead); constructors return boxed trait objects borrowing the Block. Go panics (wrong IV or nonce length, short output, input not full blocks, wrong nonce length given to GCM) are Err(cipher::Error) carrying Go's panic message; errOpen is Error::is_authentication_failure. Rust's borrow rules make Go's 'invalid buffer overlap' panics unreachable; the exact-overlap idiom is covered by the *_in_place methods, and Seal/Open append to a Vec like Go's dst. Modes accept any Block with an 8 or 16 byte block size (every Go block cipher); GCM requires 16. NewGCMWithNonceSize supports the nonce sizes in cipher::GCM_NONCE_SIZES (1-32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 56, 60, 64, 72, 80, 96, 100, 112, 120, 128, 192, 256) because the aes-gcm crate fixes the size at compile time; Go accepts any positive size. io.Closer has no Rust equivalent, so StreamWriter::close flushes the underlying writer and drops it.

AEAD.Open.note: appends to a Vec; open_in_place is Go's ciphertext[:0] idiom

AEAD.Seal.note: appends to a Vec; seal_in_place is Go's plaintext[:0] idiom

BlockMode.CryptBlocks.note: crypt_blocks_in_place covers dst equal to src

NewGCMWithNonceSize.note: Nonce sizes outside cipher::GCM_NONCE_SIZES return an error: the reviewed aes-gcm crate fixes the nonce size at compile time, and the project does not build GCM itself (ADR 0003: no first-party cryptographic constructions).

Stream.XORKeyStream.note: xor_key_stream_in_place covers dst equal to src

StreamWriter.Close.note: flushes and drops the writer: Rust has no io.Closer

StreamWriter.Write.note: impl Write for StreamWriter; a short write is an error, as in Go
